subject: Post-call: CustCorp evals & next steps (recommended models, dataset format)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@custcorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: CustCorp evals & next steps (recommended models, dataset format)

Hi Samantha - great to meet today. Quick recap + suggested next steps to get a CustCorp-specific eval running on Redwood:

Recap (1-line): You want to validate Redwood-powered assistance for loan-approval guidance across two verticals (retail and SME) with a focus on hallucination rate, policy compliance, and latency-sensitive prompts.

Recommendations / next steps:
- Recommended models to try (start fast, iterate):
  1) redwood-7b-quant (low-latency, cost-efficient) - good for high-throughput scenarios.
  2) llama3-13b-8k (higher coverage/accuracy for complex policy reasoning).
  3) redwood-13b-compat (backstop for QA-critical flows).
- Benchmarks & prompt sets: I attached a starter prompt set (custcorp_prompt_set_v1.csv) and our eval template (redwood_eval_template.json). Also linking our public benchmark summary for similar finserv workloads.
- Dataset format & scoring (what we need from you):
  * CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, category, priority, tolerance_notes.
  * For long-form responses include an expected_response snippet and a blackbox scoring rubric.
  * Scoring metrics we recommend: exact-match (EM) for policy flags, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) for free-text accuracy, and a manual pass/fail for compliance-critical items.
- Setup on Redwood: we can run an isolated eval run in your dedicated project (no data leaves your account). You can upload the dataset to the Drive link above or point us at an S3 bucket. We'll provide an eval run report (token breakdown, latency p95, per-case scoring).
- Timeline: If you can send a representative 200-500 prompt sample by EOW next week (2026-03-27), we'll run 3 model variants and share results within 4 business days of receiving data.

Next actions: If this works, reply with where you'll drop the data (Drive vs S3) and whether Procurement needs a separate kickoff (I cc'd Tom/Procurement). Rishi - tagging you for config/quantization notes and any special scoring hooks we should add. Neha - I'll coordinate scheduling for the eval run once data is in.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - this is perfect, appreciate the clear checklist. A couple quick clarifications before we share data:

1) For the expected_response column, some of our cases are multi-turn (follow-ups). Do you prefer the canonical single-best reply or an annotated multi-turn sequence?
2) For semantic-similarity scoring, what embedding model do you use for thresholding? We need to ensure this matches our internal tooling.
3) Data residency: we prefer Drive (shared folder) but want confirmation that the eval run won't persist inputs in any global logs.

I'll aim to get a 250-sample mix by 2026-03-26. Tom / Procurement - looping you in for any contracting questions; Marissa, if we need an MSA addendum for eval data handling, let me know.

- Samantha
Head of Product | CustCorp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@custcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20 21:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: CustCorp evals & next steps (recommended models, dataset format)

Great questions - quick answers on the tech/config side:

1) Multi-turn: Prefer canonical single-best reply per row for automated scoring. For cases where the follow-up matters, include an extra row with the follow-up prompt and link it via the "id" and "metadata" column (see template). If you have a small set of complex multi-turn cases we can flag them for manual review.
2) Embedding model: We compute semantic-similarity with redwood-embed-v2 (1280-d) by default. Standard cosine thresholds we use are: >=0.88 = strong match, 0.75-0.88 = tolerable, <0.75 = mismatch. We can tune thresholds to your QA.
3) Data handling: Eval runs in your project context; inputs are not used to train models and are not persisted to shared model logs. We can enable additional retention controls (7/30/90 day). If you want, we can spin the run in your Dedicated environment for extra isolation.

Notes on model configs for the run:
- redwood-7b-quant: int8, no KV-cache warmup needed. Good baseline for throughput.
- llama3-13b-8k: will likely improve policy reasoning false-negatives; expect 2x token-cost vs 7b.
- redwood-13b-compat: use as guardrail for policy-critical items; include deterministic decoding (top-p 0.6, temp 0.2) for the compliance pass.

I'll prepare a small eval config (attached) that maps metrics to output columns. Happy to discuss any custom scoring hooks you need.

- Rishi
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
